# Register a repository as a workspace

## Intent

A developer registers a git repository under a slug with one call, and the hub makes its own bare copy of that repository in the background, so that agents and people can work on it through the hub. Registration either records everything it needs (the workspace, its origin credential and the clone work) or records nothing, the credential is never readable again, and clone work survives a restart of the hub. The rules this needs — how workspace names, URLs, branch names and durations are validated, and how a route answers for a workspace that is not ready — are built once here, for every later workspace feature.

## Goals

- `POST /workspaces` with a `slug` and a `git_url` answers `201` with a workspace in `status: "pending"` and `access: "owner"`, and emits `parley.workspace.create`.
- A given origin credential is checked against origin within 10 seconds before anything is stored; a refused credential creates nothing and answers `400 credential_check_failed`.
- A stored credential is a workspace secret and appears in no response, event, log line or `clone_error`.
- Create is all-or-nothing: workspace, credential secrets, clone work and event are recorded together or not at all.
- The clone runs in the background: `pending` → `cloning` → `ready` or `failed`. A `ready` workspace has every branch and tag of origin with full history, a `default_branch`, a `head_sha` and the origin head of every branch as the ref `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` of the copy.
- A failed clone leaves `status: "failed"`, a `clone_error` without credentials and no partial copy on disk.
- Clone work that was `pending` or `cloning` when the hub stopped is taken up again at the next start, in `created_at` order.
- At most `[workspace].workers` clones run at the same time.
- One guard answers `409 workspace_busy`, `409 workspace_not_ready` or `409 workspace_archived` for a workspace that cannot serve a route that needs its repository.
- `parley workspace create` registers a repository from the shell and, with `--wait`, returns when the workspace is `ready` (exit 0) or `failed` (exit 1).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Source: `docs/prd/04_workspaces_and_forks.md`, WS-FR-001 to WS-FR-027 with §4.3.1, §4.3.4, §4.3.5, §4.5 (`POST /workspaces`), §4.6 (`parley workspace create`), §4.7.1, §4.8 (`parley.workspace.create`) and §4.9 (`[workspace].workers`).

Package 07 workspace_access_rule delivers the minimal workspace record the access rule reads (slug, owner, organization, kind, parent). This package extends that record to every field of §4.3.1 and is the first to create a workspace. It is also the first package that runs git: `internal/gitrepo/` starts here with the operations this package needs (list a remote's refs, make a bare clone, open and inspect a copy, remove a copy). Later packages add to it.

Code lives in `internal/workspace/` (record, validators, state guard, create handler, clone work), `internal/gitrepo/` (the `git` subprocess wrapper and a test helper that serves an origin), `internal/cli/workspace.go` (the command) and `test/e2e/` (end-to-end tests). The composition in `internal/hub` (package 03) wires the clone workers into the hub's start and stop.

## Requirements

All paths are relative to `/api/v1`. Errors are the error envelope of the platform conventions; "`409 conflict`" means HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict`.

### Validation rules (WS-FR-009 to WS-FR-013)

These rules are used by this package and by every later workspace package.

- **Repository slug (WS-FR-009).** 3 to 64 characters; lower-case letters `a`–`z`, digits and hyphens only; starts with a letter; ends with a letter or digit; does not contain `--`.
- **`git_url` (WS-FR-010).** Either `https://<host>/<path>` or `git@<host>:<path>`, with a non-empty host and a non-empty path. `http://`, `ssh://`, `file://` and every other form are refused. An `https` URL with userinfo (`https://user@host/…`, `https://user:pass@host/…`) is refused. The check is on the form only: no name is resolved and no connection is made.
- **Branch name (WS-FR-011).** Not empty; no control character, space, `~`, `^`, `:`, `?`, `*`, `[` or `\`; no `..`, `//` or `@{`; not exactly `@`; does not start with `-` or `/`; does not end with `/`, `.` or `.lock`; no path component that starts with `.` or ends with `.lock`.
- **Fork name (WS-FR-012).** 1 to 32 characters; lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; starts and ends with a letter or digit; no `--`.
- **Duration (WS-FR-013).** A positive whole number followed by one unit `m`, `h` or `d` (`90m`, `24h`, `7d`). `0m`, `-1h`, `1.5h`, `10`, `10s`, `1h30m` and the empty string are refused.

### State preconditions (WS-FR-007, WS-FR-008)

A route that needs the repository of a workspace asks one guard, after access and validation. The guard answers:

| Workspace | Answer | `error_type` |
|---|---|---|
| a reclone, archive or delete is running on it (the maintenance marker is set), or `status` is `pending` or `cloning` | `409` | `workspace_busy` |
| `status` is `failed` | `409` | `workspace_not_ready` |
| `status` is `archived` | `409` | `workspace_archived` |
| `status` is `ready` and no marker | passes | |

The marker is checked first. A `ready` workspace always passes, whatever other requests are running on it: there is no per-workspace lock a caller can observe, and `409 workspace_busy` is answered in the first row's cases only.

### Authentication and access on `POST /workspaces` (WS-FR-001, WS-FR-002, WS-FR-006)

The route follows the platform's check order: authentication, binding guard, scope, access, validation, state, act. The first failing check decides the answer.

- Scope: `workspaces:write`. Only personal access tokens are scope-checked. A token without it — also one that holds only `workspaces:read` — gets `403 insufficient_scope`. An API key is not scope-checked.
- An admin token cannot create a workspace, because a workspace needs a user as owner: `403 forbidden`.
- Because scope and access come before validation, a token without the scope and an admin token get their `403` also when the body is invalid.

### `POST /workspaces`: the request (WS-FR-014, WS-FR-015, WS-FR-017, WS-FR-018)

Body members, checked in this order; the first invalid one decides the message. Every failure is `400 invalid_request` unless stated, and creates nothing. Unknown members are ignored.

| Member | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `slug` | yes | string; the slug rule |
| `git_url` | yes | string; the `git_url` rule |
| `default_branch` | no | string or null; the branch-name rule. Absent or null: taken from origin when the clone completes |
| `org_id` | no | string or null; an organization id or slug. Absent or null: the caller's personal organization. An unknown organization is `400 invalid_request`. An organization the caller is not a member of is `403 forbidden` |
| `display_name` | no | string or null; at most 128 characters. Absent, null or empty: stored as the slug |
| `description` | no | string or null; at most 1024 characters. Absent or null: `""` |
| `workspace_mode` | no | string or null; `standard` or `carry_patch`. Absent, null or empty: `standard` |
| `upstream_url`, `integration_branch` | carry-patch | With `standard`: the presence of either with a non-null value is refused. With `carry_patch`: `upstream_url` is required and follows the `git_url` rule; `integration_branch`, when given, follows the branch-name rule |
| `settings` | no | object or null; applied as a settings value: any other JSON type is refused, and a key that is not a registered setting is refused with the message `unknown setting "<key>"` |
| `git_pat` | no | string, not empty; excludes `git_username` and `git_password` |
| `git_username`, `git_password` | no | strings, not empty; given together or not at all |

Any credential member needs an `https` `git_url`; with a `git@…` URL it is refused. A member of the wrong JSON type is refused. Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points).

### `POST /workspaces`: the credential check (WS-FR-016)

After validation, and only when a credential was given:

1. If the hub has no secret encryption key configured, the answer is `503 secrets_unavailable`. Origin is not contacted and nothing is created.
2. The hub lists origin's refs with the credential, with a deadline of 10 seconds. Any failure — origin refuses the credential, origin cannot be reached, the deadline passes — answers `400 credential_check_failed` and creates nothing. The message contains neither the token nor the password.

Without a credential origin is not contacted during the request; a repository that cannot be reached anonymously shows up as a failed clone.

### `POST /workspaces`: the result (WS-FR-019 to WS-FR-021, §4.3.1, §4.3.2, §4.8)

On success the hub records, in one transaction: the workspace (`kind: "repository"`, `status: "pending"`, `owner_id` the caller, the organization, the given or default fields), which is also its clone work; the credential as workspace secrets (`GIT_PAT`, or `GIT_USERNAME` and `GIT_PASSWORD`); and the event `parley.workspace.create`. If any of them cannot be stored, nothing is created and the answer is `500 internal`.

The answer is `201` with the workspace object: every field of §4.3.1, nullable ones as `null` and never omitted (`default_branch` is the given value or `null`; `head_sha`, `origin_head_sha`, `clone_error`, `last_sync_at`, `sync_error`, `upstream_head_sha`, `parent_slug`, `fork_point`, `expires_at`, `auto_change`, `purpose` and `session_id` are `null`), `created_at` and `updated_at`, and the computed fields:

- `org_slug`: the slug of the workspace's organization;
- `hub_url`: `<external_url>/git/<org_slug>/<slug>.git` with one trailing `/` of `[server].external_url` removed, or `null` when `external_url` is empty;
- `access`: `"owner"`;
- `settings`: every registered setting key with its effective value.

No member of the response carries the credential.

The event `parley.workspace.create` has `workspace` and resource the slug, the caller as actor, and metadata `kind` (`repository`), `git_url`, `workspace_mode` and `default_branch` (the given value or `null`). A refused or failed request emits no event.

A slug that is in use — by any workspace, in any status — answers `409 conflict` and changes nothing. Of two concurrent creates with the same slug, exactly one answers `201` and the other `409 conflict`.

The route creates a resource, so it accepts `Idempotency-Key` under the platform's rules.

### Git credentials for origin (§4.3.5)

Whenever the hub talks to origin for a workspace it resolves the credential anew from the workspace's secrets:

1. `GIT_PAT` is set and not empty: HTTP Basic authentication, user name `x-token-auth`, the token as password.
2. Otherwise `GIT_USERNAME` and `GIT_PASSWORD` are both set: HTTP Basic authentication with them.
3. Otherwise no credential (anonymous). A user name without a password is no credential.

A failure to read the secrets is an error; the operation that needed the credential fails and never falls back to anonymous. A credential is handed to `git` outside the URL, the command-line arguments and the copy's configuration.

### Clone (WS-FR-022 to WS-FR-024, §4.3.4)

Clone work for a `pending` workspace starts by setting `status: "cloning"` and clearing `clone_error`. It then makes a bare copy of origin with all branches and tags and full history, under `[workspace].path`.

- **Success.** The hub records `default_branch` (the one given at creation, else origin's default branch), `head_sha` (the head of that branch), the origin head of every branch as the ref `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` of the copy (so `origin_head_sha` equals `head_sha`), then sets `status: "ready"`. Commit ids are full 40-character ids.
- **Post-clone step.** A later package may register a step for a workspace mode. After a fresh clone of a workspace in that mode and before `ready`, the hub runs it. A failure of the step is logged and does not prevent `ready`.
- **Failure.** The clone fails when origin cannot be reached or refuses, when the credential cannot be read, when a `default_branch` was given and origin has no such branch (the `clone_error` names the branch), and when origin has no branch at all. The hub sets `status: "failed"` and `clone_error`, and leaves no directory at the copy's place. `clone_error` has known secret values replaced by `[redacted]`, userinfo removed from URLs, and is at most 1024 bytes. A failed clone is not retried automatically and emits no event.

### Durable clone work (WS-FR-025 to WS-FR-027, §4.7.1, §4.9)

- **Workers.** At most `[workspace].workers` clones (default 4) run at the same time; further clone work waits and is started in the order it was recorded. A value below 1 stops the start of `parleyd` with an error that names `[workspace].workers`.
- **Start.** When the hub starts, every workspace in `pending` or `cloning` is queued again in `created_at` order (then slug) before the hub listens. Leftovers of an interrupted clone are removed.
- **Existing copy.** When clone work finds a copy at the workspace's place, it checks that the copy is valid: it opens as a repository, the workspace's default branch (the copy's own default branch while the record has none) resolves to a commit, its origin is the workspace's `git_url`, and it was made for this very workspace record. A valid copy is kept: the workspace becomes `ready` with `head_sha` read from the copy, and nothing is cloned. Anything else is discarded and cloned fresh. A copy left by an earlier workspace with the same slug is therefore never adopted.
- **Shutdown.** When the hub stops, a running clone is interrupted. The workspace stays `pending` or `cloning`, nothing is left at the copy's place, and the work is resumed at the next start.

### `parley workspace create` (§4.6)

Flags: `--slug` and `--git-url` (required), `--default-branch`, `--org`, `--display-name`, `--description`, `--workspace-mode`, `--upstream-url`, `--integration-branch`, `--git-pat`, `--git-username`, `--git-password`, `--setting key=value` (repeatable), `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--poll-interval`.

- **Client checks.** Exit 2 with a `usage_error` on stderr, and no request is sent, when: `--slug` or `--git-url` is missing; `--git-pat` is given with `--git-username` or `--git-password`; one of `--git-username` and `--git-password` is given without the other; a credential flag is given with an empty value; a `--setting` has no `=` or an empty key.
- **`--setting`.** The text is split at the first `=`. An empty value is sent as `null`. Otherwise, for `protected_branches` the value is split at commas into a list of strings. Otherwise `true` and `false` are sent as booleans. Anything else is sent as a string. Of a repeated key the last one wins. The parser (`ParseSettingFlags`) is this package's and `parley workspace update` of package 11 calls it.
- **Request.** `POST /workspaces` with a body that holds a member for each flag given (`--org` as `org_id`, the settings as `settings`) and no member for a flag not given.
- **Output.** The workspace on stdout, exit 0. A hub error is printed and exits 1 by the CLI's common rules.
- **`--wait`.** After a `201` the command polls `GET /workspaces/:slug` every `--poll-interval` under `--timeout`. `ready` and `failed` are the terminal states. `ready`: the final workspace on stdout, exit 0. `failed`: the final workspace on stdout, `wait_failed` on stderr, exit 1.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Public repository.** A developer runs `parley workspace create --slug … --git-url …`; the CLI posts to the hub; `parleyd` validates, records the workspace and the event and answers `201` `pending`; a clone worker clones origin; the workspace is `ready` with origin's branches, tags and head.
2. **Private repository.** A developer posts with `git_pat`; `parleyd` lists origin's refs with the token, stores it as the secret `GIT_PAT` with the workspace and answers `201`; the clone resolves the credential from the secret and succeeds; the token is in no response, event or log line.
3. **Restart.** A workspace is `pending` when the hub stops; an operator starts the hub again; `parleyd` queues the workspace before it listens and clones it; the workspace becomes `ready`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language, git and tests (project-wide).** Go; the hub runs the `git` command (2.38 or later) as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo`, with no git library; repositories are bare repositories on disk; HTTP uses `net/http`; the CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`; the store is SQLite behind `internal/store`; tests are table-driven with `testing` and `net/http/httptest`.
2. **Clone work is the workspace row.** A workspace in `pending` is its own clone work record; there is no separate queue table. One row write makes "workspace and clone work recorded together" (WS-FR-020) true by construction, and the start-up scan of WS-FR-025 reads the same rows. Workers are woken in memory after the transaction commits; packages that put a workspace back to `pending` (package 14) call the same entry point.
3. **Where a copy lives.** `<[workspace].path>/<slug>.git`. A clone is made in a temporary directory beside it and renamed into place only when complete, so a failed or interrupted clone leaves nothing a later check could take for a valid copy. Other packages get the path from `internal/workspace`, never by building it.
4. **Recognising a copy of an earlier workspace.** Each workspace record gets a random instance id at creation, shown in no response. A finished clone writes it into the copy's git configuration (`parley.workspace`); the validity check of WS-FR-026 compares it. The PRD says such a copy is never adopted and not how it is told apart.
5. **Origin heads are refs, not rows.** The last head seen on origin for each branch is the ref `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` of the workspace's copy, as §10.3 of the source describes them and as package 12 keeps them on every sync. A finished clone writes one for every branch; `internal/gitrepo` reads and writes them (`OriginHeads`, `OriginHead`, `SetOriginHead`, `DeleteOriginHead`), and packages 12, 13 and 14 use those functions. The store keeps only `origin_head_sha`, the origin head of the default branch.
6. **Settings at creation: this package declares the registry, package 11 fills it.** Package 11 depends on this package, so this package cannot call it. `internal/workspace/settings.go` here declares the mechanism as a `SettingsRegistry` value the workspace service is built with: `RegisterSetting` (a key with its name, its default and a `Validate` function for its value), `ApplySettings(stored, raw)` (`null`, object, unknown key, a key with value `null`, and each other value judged by its key's `Validate`) and `EffectiveSettings(stored, default_branch)`. Create applies `settings` with `ApplySettings` and answers `settings` from `EffectiveSettings`, and knows no key. Package 11 registers the 21 keys of §4.3.3 through `RegisterSetting` (its `RegisterSettingKeys`, which the hub's composition calls on the registry) and owns their types, defaults, validation rules and the choice of the key an error names; once it is built, create applies those rules without a change here. With this package alone, `settings: {}` and `null` are accepted, any key is `unknown setting`, and the response shows `{}`.
7. **Carry-patch members.** WS-FR-017 is implemented as written: the mode value, `upstream_url` required for `carry_patch` and checked by the `git_url` rule, `integration_branch` checked by the branch-name rule, both refused for `standard`. `integration_branch` is stored as given (`null` when absent); its default and everything after the clone belong to package 31, which registers a post-clone step.
8. **Order of the checks inside create.** Body members in the table's order; then the organization (unknown `400`, not a member `403`); then slug in use (`409`); then the missing encryption key (`503`); then the credential check against origin (`400`); then the transaction, where a racing duplicate slug is still `409`. Cheap local refusals come before the outbound call.
9. **No credential, no check.** Without a credential the request does not contact origin; the PRD checks only "a given credential".
10. **`git_url` in the event.** `https` URLs with userinfo are refused at creation, so the stored `git_url` is emitted unchanged. The `git@` of the other form is that form's fixed login, not a credential.
11. **An origin without branches fails the clone.** The PRD is silent; a workspace needs a default branch that resolves, so the clone ends `failed` with `clone_error` `origin has no branches`.
12. **No deadline on a clone.** The PRD gives the credential check a deadline and the clone none. A clone ends by success, failure or shutdown.
13. **Empty `workspace_mode`.** An empty string means `standard`, as CP-FR-001 states for the same member.
14. **How the credential reaches git.** Through the environment of the `git` process (an askpass program fed from the environment), never in the URL, the arguments or the copy's configuration, so that no process listing, `clone_error` or stored remote URL can carry it.
15. **`--wait` works once package 11 is built.** `--wait` polls `GET /workspaces/:slug`, which package 11 delivers. Until then the poll gets `404` and the command ends with that error, as the CLI's waiting rules say for a hub error. This package tests the wait against a scripted `httptest` server; package 11 runs `parley workspace create --wait` against a real hub in its end-to-end test.
16. **Test origin.** Because `git_url` must be `https`, tests serve a bare repository over TLS from `net/http/httptest` (git's file-based HTTP transport after `git update-server-info`, with optional Basic authentication) and make the hub's `git` trust the test certificate through an environment option of `internal/gitrepo`. The helper lives in `internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest/` and is the only test origin of the repository: package 13 extends it with a mode that accepts pushes, and packages 12, 14 and 31 use it.

17. **One response encoder.** `RenderWorkspace` in `internal/workspace/response.go` is the only place a workspace object is built. Package 11 owns the object's full definition (WS-FR-029) and completes the encoder; package 15 registers a fork view with `RegisterForkView` so that a fork's computed members are shown without `internal/workspace` importing `internal/fork`.
18. **Composition.** The clone workers are built and started on the composition value of `internal/hub` (package 03), not in `cmd/parleyd`.
19. **The secret component's operations (package 39).** This package uses `internal/secret` by the names package 39 exports and adds none: `Available()` decides the `503 secrets_unavailable` refusal before origin is contacted; `Put`, given the create transaction, stores `GIT_PAT`, or `GIT_USERNAME` and `GIT_PASSWORD`, in the workspace scope of the new slug and writes no event of its own; `Get(workspace scope, slug, name)` reads each of them for credential resolution on every call and registers the value with the text scrubber. An error from `Put` rolls the create transaction back (`500 internal`); an error from `Get` is returned as an error and is never read as "no credential".

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Origin**: A registered workspace's remote (`git_url`).
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Upstream**: For a carry-patch workspace, the project it tracks (`upstream_url`).
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Durable job**: Background work that is recorded before its request returns, survives restarts and is retried with backoff. Rebuilds are the only durable jobs (§10). Clone work, restacks and land attempts are also durable but follow their own rules and are not retried with backoff (§4, §7, §8).
- **Origin head**: For a branch of a repository workspace, the last head the hub saw on origin.
- **Clone work**: The durable instruction to make or re-check the hub's copy of a workspace; a workspace in `pending` or `cloning` has clone work outstanding.
- **Maintenance marker**: The record that a reclone, archive or delete is running on a workspace.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Validation rules for workspace names, URLs, branches and durations

**Rationale:** Every workspace route judges a slug, a URL, a branch name and a duration by the same rule, so the rules are built once.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any string, accept it as a repository slug exactly when it is 3 to 64 characters long, holds only the letters a to z, digits and hyphens, starts with a letter, ends with a letter or digit and does not contain two hyphens in a row
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateSlug: accepted {abc, a1b, my-repo-2, a 64-character slug}; refused {'', ab, a 65-character slug, 1abc, -abc, abc-, a--b, Abc, a_b, a.b, 'a b', 'abç'}; assert the result per row
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any string, accept it as a git_url exactly when it has the form https://<host>/<path> without userinfo or the form git@<host>:<path>, with a non-empty host and a non-empty path, without resolving the host or opening a connection
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateGitURL: accepted {https://example.com/a/b.git, https://example.com:8443/a, git@example.com:a/b.git}; refused {'', http://example.com/a, ssh://git@example.com/a, file:///tmp/a, /tmp/a, https://example.com, https://example.com/, https:///a, https://user@example.com/a, https://user:pw@example.com/a, git@example.com:, git@:a, other@example.com:a}; assert the result per row; the host name in every row does not resolve, which proves no lookup happens
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any string, accept it as a branch name exactly when it is not empty, holds no control character, space, ~, ^, :, ?, *, [ or backslash, holds no '..', '//' or '@{', is not exactly '@', does not start with '-' or '/', does not end with '/', '.' or '.lock', and has no path component that starts with '.' or ends with '.lock'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateBranchName: accepted {main, feature/x, fix-42, a.b, a@b, release/1.2}; refused {'', '@', 'a b', a~b, a^b, a:b, a?b, a*b, a[b, a\b, a..b, a//b, a@{b, -a, /a, a/, a., a.lock, .a, a/.b, a.lock/b, a name holding a tab, a name holding byte 0x7f}; assert the result per row
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any string, accept it as a fork name exactly when it is 1 to 32 characters long, holds only the letters a to z, digits and hyphens, starts and ends with a letter or digit and does not contain two hyphens in a row
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateForkName: accepted {a, 7, a-b, 1x, a 32-character name}; refused {'', a 33-character name, -a, a-, a--b, A, a_b}; assert the result per row
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any string, parse it as a duration exactly when it is a positive whole number in decimal digits followed by one unit m, h or d, and return the length of time it names
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ParseDuration: {90m -> 90 minutes, 24h -> 24 hours, 7d -> 168 hours, 1m -> 1 minute}; refused {'', 0m, 0d, -1h, +1h, 1.5h, 10, 10s, 1h30m, h, ' 5m', 5M}; assert the value or the refusal per row
   ```

### REQ-2: State preconditions of routes that need the repository

**Rationale:** A caller must be able to tell 'come back in a moment' from 'this needs repair' from 'this is archived', and must never be refused only because someone else is working.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose maintenance marker is set or whose status is pending or cloning, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without acting
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/guard_test.go, a table over RequireReady(workspace) with rows {status, marker} -> outcome: {pending, none} -> 409 workspace_busy; {cloning, none} -> 409 workspace_busy; {ready, reclone} -> 409 workspace_busy; {failed, reclone} -> 409 workspace_busy; {ready, archive} -> 409 workspace_busy; {archived, delete} -> 409 workspace_busy; {failed, none} -> 409 workspace_not_ready; {archived, none} -> 409 workspace_archived; {ready, none} -> nil. Assert the returned error's status and error_type per row. Then call RequireReady on one ready workspace from 50 goroutines at once and assert every call returns nil
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose status is failed and whose maintenance marker is not set, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without acting
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_not_ready
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.3] IF a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose status is archived and whose maintenance marker is not set, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without acting
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_archived
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any workspace whose status is ready and whose maintenance marker is not set, let the request pass the state check, however many other requests are running on that workspace
   → the guard returns no error
   Check: same as REQ-2.1

### REQ-3: Who may call POST /workspaces

**Rationale:** A workspace needs a user as owner, and a token must hold the write scope before it can create anything.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] IF POST /workspaces is called with a personal access token that does not hold the scope workspaces:write, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create nothing
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope; no workspace exists afterwards
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   ```
   in internal/workspace/create_test.go, a table over callers posting a valid body: {PAT with no scopes, PAT with only workspaces:read} -> 403 insufficient_scope; {admin token} -> 403 forbidden; {PAT with workspaces:write} -> 201; {API key} -> 201. Then the same refused callers posting the body {} -> the same 403 and error_type, never 400. After every refused row assert the store holds no workspace and the event log no parley.workspace.create
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF POST /workspaces is called with the admin token, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create nothing
   → HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; no workspace exists afterwards
   Check: same as REQ-3.1
1. [REQ-3.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any POST /workspaces request, answer with the first failing check in the order scope, admin-token refusal, body validation, so that a caller refused by scope or as admin token gets the same 403 for a valid and for an invalid body
   → HTTP 403 with the same error_type for a valid and an invalid body
   Check: same as REQ-3.1

### REQ-4: Validation of the create request

**Rationale:** An invalid registration must be refused whole, with an answer that says which member is wrong.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] IF the body of POST /workspaces has no slug or no git_url, or one of them is not a string or breaks its validation rule, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request, naming the first invalid member in the order slug, git_url, default_branch, org_id, display_name, description, workspace_mode, upstream_url, integration_branch, settings, git_pat, git_username, git_password
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; no workspace, secret or event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   ```
   in internal/workspace/create_test.go, a table over bodies posted by U, each derived from a valid body: {no slug, slug 'ab', slug 'A-b', slug 7, no git_url, git_url 'http://example.com/a', git_url 'https://u:p@example.com/a', git_url null}; plus one body with slug 'ab' and git_url 'file:///x' whose message must name slug. Assert 400 invalid_request per row, the member name in error.message, and that the store holds no workspace and the event log is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF default_branch is present and not null and is not a valid branch name, or display_name is longer than 128 characters, or description is longer than 1024 characters, or one of the three is neither a string nor null, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request

### REQ-5: Check of a given origin credential before anything is stored

**Rationale:** A mistyped token should cost the developer one refused request, not a workspace that fails to clone minutes later.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a valid create request carries git_pat, or git_username with git_password, THE parleyd SHALL list origin's refs with that credential, under a deadline of 10 seconds, before it stores the workspace, a secret or an event
   → one ref listing against git_url with the credential; nothing is stored before it returns
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   - setup: a secret encryption key is configured
   - setup: a fake origin lister that records its arguments, its context deadline and the store's workspace count at call time
   ```
   in internal/workspace/credential_test.go: post with git_pat 'tok-123'; assert the lister was called once with the request's git_url, user name x-token-auth and password tok-123, with a context deadline between 9 and 10 seconds away, and that at the moment of the call the store held no workspace. Post with git_username 'u' and git_password 'p'; assert the lister saw u and p
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF the ref listing made with the given credential fails because origin refuses the credential, origin cannot be reached or the 10-second deadline passes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request with a message that contains neither the token nor the password, and create nothing
   → HTTP 400 with error_type credential_check_failed; the response does not contain the credential; no workspace, secret or event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   - setup: a secret encryption key is configured
   - setup: a fake origin lister whose result the test sets
   ```
   in internal/workspace/credential_test.go, a table over the lister's result: {authentication refused, connection refused, context deadline exceeded, an error whose text holds the token and https://x-token-auth:tok-123@host/}; assert 400 with error_type credential_check_failed, that the response body does not contain tok-123, and that the store holds no workspace, the secret store no entry and the event log no event. In internal/gitrepo/gitrepo_test.go: ListRemote against a listener that accepts and never answers, with a 200 ms context, returns an error within 2 seconds and leaves no git process running
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] IF a valid create request carries a credential and the hub has no secret encryption key configured, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without contacting origin and create nothing
   → HTTP 503 with error_type secrets_unavailable; origin is not contacted; no workspace, secret or event is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   - setup: no secret encryption key is configured
   - setup: a fake origin lister that records its calls
   ```
   in internal/workspace/credential_test.go: post with git_pat; assert 503 with error_type secrets_unavailable, zero lister calls, no workspace stored. Post the same body without git_pat; assert 201
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN a valid create request carries no credential member, THE parleyd SHALL answer without contacting origin
   → HTTP 201; zero requests to origin during the request
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   - setup: a fake origin lister that records its calls


### REQ-6: Registration of a repository workspace

**Rationale:** Registration is the entry to the product: it must give the caller a complete record at once and must never leave half a workspace behind.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a caller with a user identity posts a valid body to POST /workspaces with a slug that is not in use, THE parleyd SHALL record the workspace with kind repository, status pending, the caller as owner, the given or the caller's personal organization, display_name defaulting to the slug and description defaulting to the empty string, and answer with the workspace object
   → HTTP 201 with the workspace object: every field present, nullable fields null and never omitted, status pending, access owner
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
   - setup: a user U with a personal organization and an API key
   ```
   in internal/workspace/create_test.go: r = post {slug: 'demo', git_url: 'https://example.com/a.git'} as U with the clone workers stopped; assert 201; assert the body holds exactly the members of the workspace object (every field of the workspace record plus org_slug, hub_url, access, settings); assert slug demo, kind repository, workspace_mode standard, status pending, access owner, owner_id U, org_id U's personal organization, display_name demo, description '', and that default_branch, head_sha, origin_head_sha, clone_error, last_sync_at, sync_error, upstream_url, integration_branch, upstream_head_sha, parent_slug, fork_point, expires_at, auto_change, purpose and session_id are present with value null; assert created_at == updated_at in RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds. Post with display_name '' -> display_name equals the slug; with default_branch 'trunk' -> default_branch trunk
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any workspace object it returns, set org_slug to the slug of the workspace's organization, hub_url to <external_url>/git/<org_slug>/<slug>.git with one trailing slash of the configured external URL removed or to null when no external URL is configured, and settings to every setting key registered with RegisterSetting with its effective value
   → hub_url is a string of that form or null; org_slug is a string; settings is an object
   Check: unit

### REQ-7: Origin credential resolution

**Rationale:** A rotated secret must take effect at the next use, and a broken secret store must never turn a private repository into an anonymous request.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] THE parleyd SHALL resolve the origin credential of a workspace from its secrets on every use: a non-empty GIT_PAT gives Basic authentication with user name x-token-auth and the token as password; otherwise GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD, when both are set, give Basic authentication with them; otherwise no credential
   → a user name and password pair, or the value 'no credential'
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace with secrets set through the real secret component
   ```
   in internal/workspace/credential_test.go, a table over the workspace's secrets -> ResolveOriginCredential: {GIT_PAT t} -> (x-token-auth, t); {GIT_PAT t, GIT_USERNAME u, GIT_PASSWORD p} -> (x-token-auth, t); {GIT_USERNAME u, GIT_PASSWORD p} -> (u, p); {GIT_PAT '', GIT_USERNAME u, GIT_PASSWORD p} -> (u, p); {GIT_USERNAME u} -> none; {GIT_PASSWORD p} -> none; {GIT_PAT ''} -> none; {} -> none. Then change GIT_PAT from t to t2 through the secret component and assert the next call returns t2 without a restart
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF the secrets of the workspace cannot be read while the credential is resolved, THEN THE parleyd SHALL return an error to the operation that needed the credential and make no anonymous request to origin
   → a non-nil error; zero requests to origin
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/credential_test.go: with a secret reader that returns an error, ResolveOriginCredential returns a non-nil error and no credential; in internal/workspace/clone_test.go: run clone work for a pending workspace with that reader; assert the fake git runner recorded zero invocations, the workspace is failed and clone_error is not empty
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any git command it runs against origin with a credential, pass the credential to git outside the URL, outside the command-line arguments and outside the copy's configuration
   → the credential value appears in no git argument, in no URL and nowhere in the copy's directory
   Check: integration
   - setup: git 2.38 or later on PATH
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/gitrepo_test.go: serve a bare repository with gitrepotest.NewOrigin requiring Basic authentication (x-token-auth, tok-123); ListRemote and Clone with that credential succeed, and both fail without it; with a runner hook that records every argv, assert no argument of any git invocation contains tok-123; after Clone assert that neither the copy's config file nor the output of git config --list in the copy contains tok-123 and that remote.origin.url equals the origin URL without userinfo
   ```

### REQ-8: Clone of a pending workspace

**Rationale:** The hub's own copy is what every other feature works on; a workspace must end either usable or plainly failed, never in between.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN clone work starts for a workspace in status pending, THE parleyd SHALL set the status to cloning and clear clone_error before it contacts origin
   → status cloning and clone_error null while the clone runs
   Check: integration

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer registers a public repository and the hub clones it

1. **developer** runs parley workspace create --slug demo --git-url <origin URL>
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces with the slug and the git_url and the developer's API key
3. **parleyd** authenticates the caller, validates the body, records the workspace in status pending together with the event parley.workspace.create, and answers 201
4. **parley CLI** prints the workspace with status pending and access owner and exits 0
5. **parleyd** starts clone work, sets the status to cloning and makes a bare clone of origin
6. **origin** serves its branches and tags
7. **parleyd** writes origin's head of every branch as refs/remotes/origin/<name> in the copy, records default_branch and head_sha and sets the status to ready

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd with the clone workers, internal/server on a real TCP listener, internal/workspace with the real store, access, secret and event components, internal/gitrepo running the real git command, internal/cli with its real HTTP client, an origin served over TLS by gitrepotest.NewOrigin

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a temporary data directory and repository root, an external URL and 2 clone workers
- a user with an API key
- an origin with the branches main and dev and the tag v1

**End state:**

- the command printed a workspace with status pending and access owner and exited 0
- the workspace record reaches status ready with default_branch main and head_sha equal to origin's main head
- the bare copy under the repository root holds main, dev and v1 at origin's commit ids
- the event log holds one parley.workspace.create for the slug

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/workspace_create_test.go: hub = startHub(t); out, code = runCLI('workspace', 'create', '--slug', 'demo', '--git-url', origin.URL); assert code == 0 and out.status == 'pending' and out.access == 'owner' and out.hub_url ends with '/demo.git'; eventually(10s) hub.Workspaces.Get('demo').status == 'ready'; assert head_sha == origin.Head('main'); assert git for-each-ref in the copy lists main, dev, v1; assert one parley.workspace.create event
```

### PATH-2: A developer registers a private repository with a token

1. **developer** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces with slug, git_url and git_pat
2. **parleyd** lists origin's refs with the token under a 10-second deadline
3. **origin** accepts the token and answers the ref listing
4. **parleyd** stores the workspace, the secret GIT_PAT and the event in one transaction and answers 201 without the token
5. **parleyd** resolves the credential from the secret, clones origin with it and sets the status to ready
6. **developer** sends the same request for another slug with a wrong token and receives 400 credential_check_failed

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd with the clone workers, internal/workspace with the real store, secret and event components, internal/gitrepo running the real git command, an origin served over TLS by gitrepotest.NewOrigin that requires Basic authentication

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process with a secret encryption key configured and its log captured
- a user with an API key
- an origin that accepts only the user name x-token-auth with the token tok-123

**End state:**

- the first workspace is ready and its copy holds origin's branches
- the workspace has the secret GIT_PAT
- the token appears in no response body, in no event, in no log line and nowhere under the repository root
- the request with the wrong token answered 400 credential_check_failed and no second workspace exists

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/workspace_create_test.go: r = post('/workspaces', {slug: 'priv', git_url: origin.URL, git_pat: 'tok-123'}); assert r.status == 201 and 'tok-123' not in r.body; eventually ready; assert secrets list of the workspace holds GIT_PAT; assert grep of the hub log, of the events JSON and of every file under the repository root finds no 'tok-123'; r2 = post(... slug: 'priv2', git_pat: 'wrong'); assert r2.status == 400 and r2.error_type == 'credential_check_failed' and the store has no workspace priv2
```

### PATH-3: An operator restarts the hub and an interrupted clone is resumed

1. **developer** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces for an origin that answers slowly
2. **parleyd** answers 201 and starts the clone
3. **operator** stops parleyd while the clone is running
4. **parleyd** interrupts the clone, leaves nothing at the copy's place and exits
5. **operator** starts parleyd again on the same data directory
6. **parleyd** queues the workspace before it listens, clones origin and sets the status to ready

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd with its start and stop sequence, internal/workspace with the real store, internal/gitrepo running the real git command, an origin served over TLS by gitrepotest.NewOrigin

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process with a temporary data directory and repository root
- an origin whose handler blocks until the test releases it

**End state:**

- after the stop the workspace record is pending or cloning and the repository root holds no entry for the slug
- after the second start, with no further request, the workspace is ready with origin's head

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/workspace_create_test.go: post create; eventually status == 'cloning'; hub.Stop(); assert status in the store is pending or cloning and no directory for the slug or temporary directory exists; origin.Release(); hub2 = startHub(t, sameDataDir); eventually(10s) status == 'ready' and head_sha == origin.Head('main')
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/gitrepo/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `07` — extends the minimal workspace record of the access rule and uses its caller identity and access levels
- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `39` — stores the origin credential as workspace secrets inside the create transaction and reads it back for every clone
- `52` — writes the event parley.workspace.create in the same transaction as the workspace

## Tasks

### 1. Validate slugs, git URLs, branch names, fork names and durations (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/validate_test.go and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Create the package internal/workspace with the exported validators ValidateSlug, ValidateGitURL, ValidateBranchName and ValidateForkName, each returning nil or an error whose text says which rule the value breaks, and ParseDuration returning a time.Duration or an error
- 1.3 ValidateSlug: 3 to 64 characters, only a to z, digits and hyphens, first character a letter, last a letter or digit, no two hyphens in a row
- 1.4 ValidateGitURL: accept https://<host>/<path> with a non-empty host and a non-empty path after the slash and no userinfo, and git@<host>:<path> with a non-empty host and path; refuse every other scheme and form; decide on the text alone, without a DNS lookup or a connection
- 1.5 ValidateBranchName: apply every clause of the branch-name rule of the PRD's Validation rules section, including control characters, the forbidden characters and sequences, the single character @, the start and end rules and the rule for each path component
- 1.6 ValidateForkName: 1 to 32 characters, only a to z, digits and hyphens, first and last character a letter or digit, no two hyphens in a row
- 1.7 ParseDuration: decimal digits naming a whole number above zero, then exactly one of m, h or d, where d is 24 hours; refuse signs, fractions, spaces, upper-case units, other units and compound values
- 1.8 Count lengths in Unicode code points and refuse any character outside the allowed set, non-ASCII letters included

**Touches:**

- `internal/workspace/validate.go`
- `internal/workspace/validate_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 2. Hold the full workspace record and guard routes by its state (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/guard_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Extend the workspace record that package 07 delivers to every field of the PRD's workspace data model: workspace_mode, git_url, default_branch, status, display_name, description, head_sha, origin_head_sha, clone_error, last_sync_at, sync_error, upstream_url, integration_branch, upstream_head_sha, fork_point, expires_at, auto_change, purpose, session_id, the stored settings document, created_at and updated_at, plus two fields no response shows: a random instance id set at creation and a maintenance marker that is empty or names the running operation (reclone, archive, delete)
- 2.3 Add the columns through a schema migration registered with internal/store, with slug unique across all workspaces; the stored settings document is one JSON column of the record; origin heads get no table, they are refs of the copy (task 5)
- 2.4 Add the status type with the values pending, cloning, ready, failed and archived, and store functions to insert a workspace, read one by slug, and update its clone fields, each usable inside a caller's store transaction
- 2.5 Add RequireReady(workspace): return the error for HTTP 409 workspace_busy when the maintenance marker is set or the status is pending or cloning, 409 workspace_not_ready when the status is failed, 409 workspace_archived when it is archived, and nil when it is ready with no marker; check the marker first
- 2.6 Raise the three errors through the error helper of internal/server so that they leave the hub as the error envelope
- 2.7 Take no lock in the guard and keep no per-workspace mutex anywhere in the package: a ready workspace passes however many requests run on it

**Touches:**

- `internal/workspace/record.go`
- `internal/workspace/store.go`
- `internal/workspace/guard.go`
- `internal/workspace/guard_test.go`

- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 3. Register a repository workspace with POST /workspaces (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3, REQ-6.1, REQ-6.2, REQ-6.4, REQ-6.5, REQ-6.6

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/create_test.go and confirm they fail, with a helper that builds the service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components and a user with an API key
- 3.2 Add the workspace service, built from the store, the organization lookup, the secret component, the event component, the configured external URL and an origin lister, and register POST /workspaces with internal/server as a route that needs the scope workspaces:write, creates a resource (so it takes Idempotency-Key) and is not workspace-scoped
- 3.3 Refuse a caller that is the admin token with 403 forbidden after the scope check and before the body is validated
- 3.4 Read slug and git_url from the body and validate them with the validators of task 1; ignore members the route does not define
- 3.5 Resolve the organization: without org_id the caller's personal organization
- 3.6 In one store transaction insert the workspace (kind repository, status pending, owner the caller, display_name the slug when absent, null or empty, description the empty string when absent or null, a fresh instance id) and write the event parley.workspace.create through the event component with the slug as workspace and resource, the caller as actor and the metadata kind, git_url, workspace_mode and default_branch; the pending row is the clone work, there is no separate queue record
- 3.7 Answer a slug that is in use with 409 conflict: look it up before the transaction, and map the unique-key violation of a racing insert to the same 409
- 3.8 Answer any other storage failure with 500 internal after rolling the transaction back, so that no workspace, secret or event remains
- 3.9 Build the workspace response object in one encoder, RenderWorkspace(record, access level) in internal/workspace/response.go, which every later package returns a workspace through and which calls a fork view registered with RegisterForkView (package 15) for a record of kind fork: every record field with nullable ones written as null, org_slug, hub_url as <external URL without one trailing slash>/git/<org_slug>/<slug>.git or null when no external URL is configured, access as the caller's level, and settings as the result of EffectiveSettings
- 3.10 Declare the settings mechanism in internal/workspace/settings.go as a SettingsRegistry value the workspace service is built with, holding no key: RegisterSetting(SettingKey), where a SettingKey has a name, a default function of the workspace's default_branch and a Validate function for a non-null JSON value; ApplySettings(stored document, raw JSON value) returning the new stored document or an invalid-request error; and EffectiveSettings(stored document, default_branch) returning every registered key with its stored value or its default. Package 11 registers the 21 keys through RegisterSetting and owns their validation rules; the tests of this package build the service with an empty registry
- 3.11 After the transaction commits, tell the clone workers about the slug through an interface that task 7 implements; answer 201 with the object

### 4. Refuse invalid create requests (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/create_test.go and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Validate the body members in the order slug, git_url, default_branch, org_id, display_name, description, workspace_mode, upstream_url, integration_branch, settings, git_pat, git_username, git_password; answer the first invalid one with 400 invalid_request and a message that names the member
- 4.3 Refuse a member whose JSON type is not the one the PRD's request table gives; accept null wherever the table says 'or null' and treat it as absent
- 4.4 default_branch: the branch-name rule; display_name at most 128 and description at most 1024 Unicode code points
- 4.5 workspace_mode: absent, null or empty means standard; any other string than standard and carry_patch is refused; with standard a non-null upstream_url or integration_branch is refused; with carry_patch upstream_url is required and follows the git_url rule and integration_branch, when given, follows the branch-name rule and is stored as given, null when absent
- 4.6 org_id: look the value up as an organization id, then as a slug; unknown is 400 invalid_request; an organization the caller is not an active member of is 403 forbidden
- 4.7 settings: null and absent mean defaults; any other non-object value is 400; apply any other value with ApplySettings starting from the empty stored document, all-or-nothing: an unregistered key is 400 with the message unknown setting "<key>", a key with value null is removed from the stored document, and every other value must pass the Validate function its key was registered with; store only the keys that were set. Create calls no other settings rule, so the rules package 11 registers apply to create without a change here
- 4.8 Credential members: git_pat excludes git_username and git_password; user name and password come together; an empty string is refused; any credential with a git_url of the git@ form is refused
- 4.9 Run every one of these checks before the slug-in-use check and before any call to origin, and leave the store, the secret component and the event log untouched on a refusal

**Touches:**

- `internal/workspace/create.go`
- `internal/workspace/settings.go`
- `internal/workspace/create_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 5. Run git against origin and resolve the origin credential (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Depends on:** 2

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/gitrepo/gitrepo_test.go and confirm they fail and to internal/workspace/credential_test.go
- 5.2 Create internal/gitrepo: a runner that executes the git command as a subprocess under a context, with a fixed minimal environment plus extra variables given as an option, terminal prompts disabled, and stderr captured into the returned error; when the context ends it kills the process and its children and waits for them
- 5.3 Hand a credential to git only through the process environment: an askpass program (the parleyd binary itself or a script written to a private temporary file) that prints the user name and the password it reads from environment variables; never place the credential in the URL, in an argument or in the repository's configuration
- 5.4 Add ListRemote(ctx, url, credential) returning origin's branches, tags and default branch, Clone(ctx, url, credential, directory) making a bare clone with all branches and tags and full history, and on an opened copy: the default branch, the commit a branch resolves to, the list of branches with their heads, the origin URL, reading and writing one configuration value, and the origin heads as the refs refs/remotes/origin/<name>: OriginHeads (every branch with its commit id), OriginHead(branch), SetOriginHead(branch, commit id) and DeleteOriginHead(branch); add Remove(directory)
- 5.5 Add the test helper package internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest: NewOrigin(t) builds a bare repository with git init in t.TempDir(), lets the test add branches, tags and commits, runs git update-server-info and serves the directory over TLS with net/http/httptest, with optional Basic authentication, a request counter and a handler gate that can block; this helper is the one test origin of the repository, which package 13 extends with a mode that accepts pushes; it returns the URL and the environment variables (the certificate file for GIT_SSL_CAINFO) that make the hub's git trust it
- 5.6 In internal/workspace add ResolveOriginCredential(ctx, workspace): read the workspace's secrets on every call with Get(workspace scope, slug, name) of internal/secret (package 39), one call per name; a non-empty GIT_PAT gives user name x-token-auth with the token; otherwise GIT_USERNAME with GIT_PASSWORD when both are set; otherwise no credential; a read error is returned as an error and never turned into 'no credential'

### 6. Check a given credential against origin and store it as workspace secrets (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5, REQ-6.3, REQ-6.7

- 6.4 Then call the lister with the git_url and the credential (git_pat as user name x-token-auth) under a context with a 10-second deadline; on any error answer 400 with error_type credential_check_failed and a fixed message that does not include the error text of git, the token or the password

### 7. Clone a pending workspace to ready or failed (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-8

**Depends on:** 3, 5

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/clone_test.go and confirm they fail
- 7.2 Add RepoPath(workspace) returning <repository root>/<slug>.git; no other package builds this path
- 7.3 Add the clone work function for one slug: in one store write move the workspace from pending to cloning and clear clone_error; do nothing for a workspace in any other status than pending or cloning
- 7.4 Resolve the origin credential (task 5); a resolution error fails the clone without running git
- 7.5 Clone origin into a temporary directory inside the repository root whose name carries a fixed prefix that no slug can have, then read the copy's branches: fail with clone_error 'origin has no branches' when there is none, and with a clone_error that names the branch when a default_branch was given at creation and the copy has no such branch
- 7.6 On success write refs/remotes/origin/<name> at the head of every branch of the copy with SetOriginHead and the workspace's instance id into the copy's configuration under the key parley.workspace, rename the temporary directory to RepoPath, and in one store transaction record default_branch (the given one, else origin's default branch), head_sha and origin_head_sha
- 7.7 When a post-clone step is registered for the workspace's mode (a registry keyed by workspace_mode that package 31 fills), run it now with the workspace still in cloning; log an error it returns and continue
- 7.8 Set the status to ready
- 7.9 On any failure remove the temporary directory and anything at RepoPath, pass the error text through the text scrubber of package 03 (secret values to [redacted], userinfo removed from URLs, at most 1024 bytes) with the resolved credential registered as a secret value, and set status failed with that clone_error; write no event and schedule no retry

### 8. Run clone work durably with a bounded number of workers (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-9

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the task's behaviours as table-driven tests to internal/workspace/worker_test.go and confirm they fail
- 8.2 Add the clone workers: a constructor that takes the number of workers and returns an error containing '[workspace].workers' when it is below 1; an Enqueue(slug) that appends to a first-in-first-out queue; exactly that many goroutines that take slugs from the queue and run the clone work function of task 7
- 8.3 Add Start: delete every temporary clone directory in the repository root, then read all workspaces in status pending or cloning ordered by created_at and then slug and enqueue them, and only then return
- 8.4 Before cloning, check what lies at RepoPath: keep it when it opens as a repository, the workspace's default branch (the copy's own default branch while the record has none) resolves to a commit, its origin URL equals git_url and its parley.workspace value equals the workspace's instance id; then record head_sha from the copy, record default_branch when the record has none, set ready, and contact origin not at all; the post-clone step does not run for a kept copy
- 8.5 Discard anything else found at RepoPath (a file, an empty directory, a repository that fails one of the four tests) and clone fresh
- 8.6 Add Stop(ctx): stop taking work, cancel the context of every running clone so that git is killed, remove the temporary directories, leave the status of interrupted workspaces as it is, and return when the goroutines have ended or the context is done
- 8.7 Implement the notification interface of task 3 with Enqueue, and export Enqueue for the packages that put a workspace back to pending
